definition: sense-perception — faculty of discrimination that alongside phantasia and thought can present objects to desire and supply the minor premise of the practical syllogism.
Soul is cause in three senses: efficient (source of movement), final (for-the-sake-of-which), formal (essence).
The fourfold scheme: material, formal, efficient, final
alteration — bodily change (heating/chilling) that mediates between psychological states and locomotion; imaginations produce the same bodily effects as real objects.
starting-point — the initial term from which the recollective search proceeds; the middle of a series is the optimal starting-point for search in both directions.
time — the necessary condition of memory: all memory implies the lapse of time; recollection involves perception of time as magnitude.
colour — the limit of the transparent in a determinately bounded body; white and black are the extremes, intermediate colours arise by ratio-mixture.
Three-grade schema: first potentiality (capacity to learn), second potentiality/first actuality (hexis), second actuality (active exercise). Body is matter = potentiality.
One of three principles; positive determination; formal cause; nature more properly
likeness — the relational aspect of the φάντασμα: when the soul perceives the image qua related to something else, it functions as a likeness and enables memory.

In Rhetoric III.11: the representation of things as active or alive, the mechanism by which metaphor produces visualization. Homer paradigmatic. Distinct from but related to the metaphysical sense (Met. Theta: being-at-work).

barnes_translation: fulfillment, actuality, fulfilment, being-at-work-staying-itself, complete reality
definition: Technical term for soul's relation to body; soul is first actuality (possession, hexis) distinguished from second actuality (exercise, energeia).
The rhetorical syllogism/deduction; the body of persuasion; drawn from probabilities and signs using fewer premises than a full syllogism. Literally 'something held in the mind.'

First technical proof: persuasion through the speaker's character as projected in the speech itself, not prior reputation. Three sources: phronesis, arete, eunoia. Character types by age and fortune in II.12-17. Heidegger reads existentially as 'way of being disposed.'
Central phenomenon of Book I; change from non-subject to subject (not motion proper)
Rhetoric is a hexis (settled capacity). Virtues are hexeis. The orator's character is a hexis that must be projected through speech.
Body is matter/potentiality to soul's form/actuality; sense receives form without matter; plants affected by forms with matter (hence no perception).
The persisting element in all becoming; identified with matter by analogy
movement, locomotion — change of place; the specific kind of change investigated in this treatise; requires both internal immovable point and external immovable ground.

The manner of linguistic expression; the second of three points of study in speech-making (after invention, before arrangement). Excellence = clarity + distinction through metaphor. Distinct from poetic diction.

barnes_translation: formula, account, definition, ratio, proof by the speech itself, argument, speech, reason, word, form
definition: Multiple senses in DA: (1) enmattered accounts (logoi enuloi) of psychic states, (2) sense-organ as a logos/ratio between contraries, (3) sense receives form 'according to its logos', (4) voice as sound with logos (meaning).
magnitude — every sensible object is a magnitude; the distance from which it can be perceived is determinate.

The transfer of an alien name to a thing; the supreme instrument of prose style. Gives clearness, charm, and distinction. Implies intuitive perception of similarity in dissimilars. Unteachable. Must be drawn from kindred things. Materials beautiful to sense. Achieves highest effect via energeia (pro ommaton poiein).
Used alongside eidos; tends toward visible/external shape

barnes_translation: thought, mind, intellect, understanding, reason, intelligence
definition: The thinking part of the soul; impassible, unmixed, capable of receiving intelligible forms; divided into active (separable, immortal) and passive (perishable).

desire — the genus of motivating states encompassing appetite (ἐπιθυμία), spirit (θυμός), and wish (βούλησις); the proximate efficient cause of all animal locomotion; 'the last in the chain of things moved to move something else' (701a1).
Nature always in a substance; substance has no contrary (hence no motion in substance)

All those feelings that so change men as to affect their judgements, and that are also attended by pain or pleasure. Second technical proof. Twelve-emotion catalogue in II.2-11. Heidegger reads as Befindlichkeit.

Movement resulting from actual exercise of a power of sense; capacity to produce and retain images in the absence of the sensed object. Subdivided into sensitive (all animals) and deliberative (calculative animals only).

barnes_translation: image, appearance, mental image, representation, phantasm
definition: image — the sensory image serving as the medium of memory; functions dually as an object of contemplation in itself (θεώρημα) and as a likeness (εἰκών) of the thing remembered.
Motion in respect of place; the primary kind of motion
One of three sources of trust in the speaker's character. Roberts: 'good sense.' Loses technical Aristotelian meaning from NE VI.
Internal principle of motion and rest; dual sense as matter and form

barnes_translation: means of persuasion, proof, mode of persuasion, trust
definition: The means by which persuasion is effected; divided into technical (entechnoi: ethos, pathos, logos) and non-technical (atechnoi: laws, witnesses, contracts, tortures, oaths). Kennedy: 'means of persuasion'; Roberts: 'modes of persuasion'.

barnes_translation: setting before the eyes, making visible, bringing before the eyes
definition: Metaphor that represents things in a state of activity (energeia), producing visualization in the audience. The culmination of the metaphor theory. Homer paradigmatic: giving metaphorical life to lifeless things.

barnes_translation: in relation to one, focal meaning

definition: sound — all sounds arise from the impact of air against bodies or bodies against air; qualitative differences determined by the physical properties of the sound-producing organs and the transmitting air.
The faculty of observing in any given case the available means of persuasion; counterpart of dialectic; universal faculty belonging to no definite science; offshoot of dialectic and ethical studies.
Absence of form; per accidens principle; essence of the infinite
The ordering of the parts of a speech; third point of study. Only prothesis and pistis strictly necessary.
Rhetoric is a techne: a systematic, teachable faculty. Yet metaphor (its supreme tool) cannot be taught. Art must conceal itself. Tension between systematic teachability and natural genius.
Nature acts for an end; all natural bodies are organs of soul. Two senses: end achieved, and being in whose interest.
That which always has something outside it; exists only potentially and by division; essence is privation
Indivisible boundary of time; same in substratum, different in being; connects and divides

barnes_translation: being as being, being qua being

definition: That whose parts share a common boundary; infinitely divisible; nothing continuous composed of indivisibles
Soul as formal cause; the essence is identical with the cause of its being.
Argumentative 'places' from which enthymemes are constructed. Common topoi apply across all species; special topoi belong to particular subjects. Twenty-eight lines of enthymeme (II.23) are topoi.

barnes_translation: the transparent, the translucent, the diaphanous
common sense, central sense, unifying sense
affections of the soul, passions of the soul
that for the sake of which, final cause
the primary perceptive faculty, common sense
